## Description

Courts often decide questions of great political consequence, yet their judges are rarely elected and they rely on other branches of government for enforcement and funding. This module studies courts as political institutions. It asks why political actors create and empower courts, how judges make decisions, how courts relate to the litigants, governments and publics who use, constrain or support them, and what effect their rulings have. The approach is comparative, covering domestic and international courts in democracies and autocracies worldwide, and draws on state-of-the-art empirical research in political science and related disciplines.
